analysis.title: Americas Transportation: Airlines - GS Fare Study: Acceleration in fares across most regions this fall despite some choppiness from comps; holiday trends strong
key_insights: GS proprietary fare study shows a broad-based pickup in fares this fall across most regions. Strengthening was first seen in the domestic US in early September, in the transatlantic in mid-September and on routes to Latin America in mid-October.

US YoY fares were strong in September, then decelerated in October with some weeks down YoY, as the industry lapped a particularly strong October 2025. Domestic fares have reaccelerated into November as comps ease (lapping the November 2025 FAA flight restrictions that disrupted demand).

Transatlantic fares were strong in September and October but have declined YoY from late October into November as comparisons get tougher. Latin America fares have accelerated YoY into November on similar comps.
Holiday trackers (16 weeks to departure) point to strong demand: Thanksgiving fares are up 42% and Christmas fares up 63% YoY on average for the weeks tracked to date, versus Labor Day fares up 24%.

Latin America has been the strongest region this fall. The acceleration in October on similar YoY comps to September points to a true acceleration in pricing. The most recent week decelerated, driven mainly by Buenos Aires to Miami fares, which shows the effect of the small sample.
The Pacific is the exception to the fall pickup, with fairly steady fare performance since the summer.

Domestic route detail is mixed. Select transcontinental routes and mid-continental routes from Chicago O'Hare are weaker, but trends are inconsistent: NYC (JFK/EWR) to SFO weak over the last month but up this week, NYC to LAX up strongly, Boston to LAX down and Boston to SFO up. LaGuardia to O'Hare shows the highest YoY 4-week fare increase.

GS cautions the study covers a small sample of routes tracking close-in fares only, and YoY fare changes do not closely track industry unit revenue changes. The directionality of the fare trends has historically corresponded with RASM trends.

sector_views.rationale: The fare study shows a broad fall acceleration in fares and strong holiday pricing, but the report states no formal sector stance and notes comp-driven choppiness and a small sample.

risk_factors: The fare study uses a small sample of routes and tracks close-in fares only, and YoY fare changes do not closely track industry unit revenue YoY changes.
Tougher YoY comparisons are pressuring transatlantic fares, which have declined YoY from late October into November.
Week-to-week volatility in the study is high, and a few routes (for example Buenos Aires to Miami) can swing regional averages.

theme_stances.key_argument: Fares accelerated across most regions this fall and holiday fares are up sharply YoY, and fare directionality has historically corresponded with RASM trends.
theme_stances.evidence: directionality of the YoY trends in our fare study have historically corresponded with changes in RASM trends
